sources.title: FoodMap v0.1 food-component annotations
sources.quality_note: Legacy curated baseline. Individual annotations retain evidence_type and notes but are not all externally cited.

sources.title: FoodMap v0.3 Korean food dictionary expansion
sources.quality_note: Fifty additional Korean foods, aliases, components, and reviewed probability annotations. This is an auditable coverage expansion, not an independent population recipe-frequency dataset.

sources.title: FoodMap v0.3 high-uncertainty recipe collection queue
sources.quality_note: A reviewable sampling plan derived from the uncertainty inventory. It is not observation data and must not update posterior probabilities.

sources.title: 10000 Recipe public recipe pages: FoodMap pilot observations
sources.quality_note: Ten user-authored public recipe pages normalized only to FoodMap component IDs. The rows retain page URLs and author-level independence groups, use a low 0.35 weight, and remain pending_review until human verification. Recipe text and images are not copied into this repository.

sources.title: MFDS Food Nutrient Database
sources.quality_note: Use for Korean nutrient values and official food-code links; record the downloaded release and retrieval date per import.

sources.title: FoodOn: A farm to fork ontology
sources.quality_note: Use for ontology categories, ingredients, processes, and cross-domain identifiers; it is not a substitute for Korean nutrient values.

sources.citation: Gardiner C, et al. The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Medicine Reviews. 2023;69:101764.
sources.quality_note: Supports direction and timing scope for the synthetic late-caffeine sleep prior, not a personalized clinical estimate.

sources.citation: Zeevi D, et al. Personalized Nutrition by Prediction of Glycemic Responses. Cell. 2015;163(5):1079-1094.
sources.quality_note: Supports individual variability in postprandial glucose responses; FoodMap uses it only with CGM-compatible outcomes.

sources.citation: The Effects of Sodium Reduction and the DASH Diet on Ambulatory Blood Pressure. 2026.
sources.quality_note: Supports the direction of the synthetic sodium-blood-pressure prior; a valid blood-pressure measurement is required.

sources.citation: Huang Y, et al. Dietary sugar consumption and health: umbrella review. BMJ. 2023;381:e071609.
sources.quality_note: Separates dietary-sugar exposures such as sugar-sweetened beverages, added sugar, and fructose. Use exposure-specific rows rather than one generic sugar effect.

sources.citation: Sugar-Sweetened Beverages and Adverse Human Health Outcomes: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses of Observational Studies. 2024.
sources.quality_note: Treat sugar-sweetened beverages as a separate exposure from total sugar. Observational evidence supports association modeling, not individual causal predictions.

sources.citation: Naghshi S, et al. Dietary intake of total, animal, and plant proteins and risk of all cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality. BMJ. 2020;370:m2412.
sources.quality_note: Retain total, animal, and plant protein as distinct exposure or food-source features; do not reduce them to protein_rich alone.

sources.citation: Godos J, et al. Dairy foods and health: an umbrella review of observational studies. International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition. 2020;71(2):138-151.
sources.quality_note: Model dairy product type and fat content separately where available. Region, product definition, and dietary confounding limit a single dairy-wide conclusion.

sources.citation: Impact of sodium intake on blood pressure, mortality and major cardiovascular events: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses. 2025.
sources.quality_note: Sodium should be stored as a dose-bearing nutrient feature and paired with measurement-aware blood-pressure outcomes, not only as a high_sodium tag.

sources.citation: Ramezani F, et al. Dietary fiber intake and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. Clinical Nutrition. 2024;43(1):65-83.
sources.quality_note: Store total fiber grams alongside fiber type and food source when those attributes are available; a fiber_rich tag alone loses important exposure detail.

sources.citation: Lane MM, et al. Ultra-processed food exposure and adverse health outcomes: umbrella review of epidemiological meta-analyses. BMJ. 2024;384:e077310.
sources.quality_note: Ultra-processed food is a processing classification. Preserve it as an exposure feature with observational-evidence limitations; do not encode it as a causal clinical effect.

sources.citation: GBD 2017 Diet Collaborators. Health effects of dietary risks in 195 countries, 1990-2017. Lancet. 2019;393:1958-1972.
sources.quality_note: Use to prioritize dietary-risk concepts in the ontology, not to assign person-level effect sizes.

sources.title: FoodMap v0.3 representative component priors
sources.quality_note: Records population-level representative components for ambiguous composite foods. It is a reviewable prior for parser output, not a recipe database or nutrient-value source.

sources.title: FoodMap v0.3 Korean composite-food component training examples
sources.quality_note: Fourteen human-curated seed examples for the trainable text classifier. The model also uses separately marked weak labels derived from SRC_FOODMAP_CURATED_V01 and SRC_FOODMAP_CURATED_V03_EXPANSION; neither source may be used as its own evaluation set.

sources.title: FoodMap v0.3 synthetic FoodMap generator
sources.quality_note: Produces synthetic pipeline-validation records only; generated response scores are not clinical measurements.
